Can a pillar in front of an exit get more people out?
In a panic, the crowd squeezes into a locked arch at the door. In one minute, only 47 get out.
Add one pillar, just off-centre. It takes the push from behind, and 59 get out.
Too close, and the gap gets too narrow. The pillar becomes the bottleneck. Just 18.
Too far back, and the crowd closes in again. The arch locks. 40.
Back in the right spot, everyone is out in two minutes thirty-eight, instead of three minutes six.
Same people. Same door. Just one pillar.
This is the pillar paradox. The right obstacle speeds up the exit.
